repos/kacxx/dev-flow/issues/47.body:
## Problem

When every ticket on an idea is closed, the source issue stays open, and no skill closes it:

- `to-tickets` says the source issue "isn't closed or rewritten" (`skills/to-tickets/SKILL.md:125`).
- `status` reports the stage "done" and suggests that the owner close #N, but it doesn't close it.

Done ideas build up as open issues unless the owner remembers to close each one by hand. Found while reviewing #45 (gap 5).

## Idea

When an idea is done, its source issue gets closed, with the owner's agreement if they want to give it.

## Open questions

1. Who closes it: `status` as a mechanical fix offered for the owner's yes, flow 2 when it closes the last ticket, or the owner alone (and this issue is closed as won't-fix)?
2. Does closing need the owner's yes, or is it safe to do automatically once every sub-issue is closed?
3. Does the closing comment list the tickets and PRs that delivered it?

Path: short — a small change once the owner and the approval rule are decided.

repos/kacxx/dev-flow/pulls?state=closed&.title: proposal: a fresh code review of the doc PR before saying yes (0.12.1)
repos/kacxx/dev-flow/pulls?state=closed&.body:
Refs #59. #59 stays open and parked: its D1 records this as a process step, and the `settle` challenge is deferred.

**Why:** `/code-review` on kacxx/aside-jot#112 found four design gaps that `proposal`'s fact-check had missed: the release model, version skew, an untested version match, and an instruction D7 made impossible to follow. The reviews on #36, #39 and #55 found the same kind of thing. The fact-check checks what the doc *says*; a fresh review asks what *happens* when the design meets real use. A reminder at the right moment costs one command, where automating it would need a new skill step, a fallback for other environments, and evals.

**Change:**
- **`proposal`:**
  - the description no longer claims design-doc reviews. It writes and fact-checks the doc, and "a fresh review of the doc PR checks the design";
  - the opening says the same;
  - the hand-off's **Blocking now** asks the owner for a fresh code review of the doc PR (such as `/code-review`) before saying yes, with findings answered as `settle` questions or wording fixes.
- **`status`:** for a decided doc PR, the owner's step is now "run a fresh code review (such as `/code-review`) on X, then merge it", so the two skills agree.
- **README:** "`proposal` checks the facts; a fresh code review of the doc PR checks the design", replacing the old "use it instead of `/code-review`", and the same in "What you answer back".
- **Eval:** a new `review-step` grader on `proposal-decided`. With the plugin, all 3 answers name the review before the yes; the baseline, 0 of 3.
- 0.12.1.

**Known gap**, recorded in #59 D1: short-path ideas have no doc PR, so this step doesn't reach them.

Tests: 6 of 6 test files pass.

repos/kacxx/dev-flow/pulls?state=closed&.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"kacxx"} -->
_Requested by **Kevin** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01MDcPXan8ZPVYF9Tu5iW7yq?thread=cmsg_01MDcPXan8ZPVYF9Tu5iW7yqKH7asP1SS2xWWksHNTzP2w)_

Before: `status` listed each relabelling fix under **Your decisions** and, separately, offered the agent's step under **Then**, each needing its own yes. `status` wasn't in the account-skill build, and the ZIPs carried test files and fixtures (about 664 KB for `status`).

After: `status` offers all pending approvals as one batch under **Your decisions**: the agent's steps plus the fixes, each naming every write it would make. Owner steps (merge a PR, close an issue) stay under **Blocking now** and are never in the batch. With 2–4 items it's one multi-select; with one item, more than four, or no multi-select, it's a numbered list answered "1, 3", "all" or "none". Then it carries out the chosen items. The selection is the yes only for writes named in full; `to-tickets`, `proposal` and ticket edits after a revision still show their draft first, and `grill` still asks its questions. `status` is in the default account-skill set, and no account-skill ZIP carries `test_*.py` or `scripts/fixtures/`.

How: `state.py` now prints a `batch` (agent steps then fixes, each with `writes` and `shows_draft`), so "every item names its writes" and "owner steps are left out" are unit-tested against every fixture. `SKILL.md` steps 2–3 describe how the batch is asked and carried out. `build_account_skills.py` gets `DEFAULT_SET` (adds `status`) and skips test files and `scripts/fixtures/`, with unit tests. There are three new eval cases: `status-batch` (numbered list, writes named, owner step left out), `status-batch-shorthand` ("1, 3" runs only #38 and #41) and `status-batch-draft` (a content-producing item still shows its draft). The eval-prompt test now checks every `status-*` prompt against the fixture it names. `status-next-action`'s empty-parts grader no longer expects **Your decisions** to be empty, because the #95 state now has a batch item. Plugin is now 0.11.0.

The evals weren't run in this session (`claude plugin eval` isn't available here), and README changes ship separately as the ticket says.

Implements D6 and D9 of docs/proposals/status.md.
Closes #39

_Requested by **Kevin** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01MDcPXan8ZPVYF9Tu5iW7yq?thread=cmsg_01MDcPXan8ZPVYF9Tu5iW7yqAAzXkFtqYt7SF1iQJEyDUH)_

Before: `status` named the stage and the next action, but it never read review comments, and a ticket whose blockers had all closed stayed without `ready-for-agent` until someone noticed. On #35 that happened today: #37 closed, and #38, #40 and #41 were labelled by hand.

After: `status` lists the comments on the source issue posted since dev-flow last wrote there, first under "blocking now". It offers adding `ready-for-agent` to each open ticket whose `Blocked by:` names issues that have all closed, with the write named, and runs it only on the owner's yes. It never offers that while a revision is in progress, nor for a `Blocked by: None` ticket with no label (the aside-jot#97 pause) or a `needs-decision` one.

How: `state.py` gains `last_write`, `review_comments` and `fixes`, and stays GET-only (a test checks every `gh` call it makes). dev-flow's last write is the latest of: the `## Decisions (grill, …)` comment, an open doc PR's opening, a merged doc PR's merge, or a ticket's creation; with none, the issue's creation. A blocker outside the sub-issues is read with one more GET. `SKILL.md` gets a step 3 for applying the fixes the owner said yes to.

Defaults I picked where D2 and D4 don't say:
- D4 defines a doc PR as an open one for the stage, but for "dev-flow's last write" I count merged doc PRs too. Otherwise, once a revision like aside-jot#100 merges, the review comment it answered would show up again as unanswered. That costs one extra read: the closed PR list.
- flag-decision's pointer comment ("D2 flagged by #97 …") is dev-flow's own, so it isn't listed as a review comment.
- A `needs-decision` ticket is never offered the relabel, because it waits on `grill`.

Fixtures:
- New, `in-progress-blockers-closed`: dev-flow#35 recorded today and rewound to just before the hand relabelling. The fix is offered for #38, #40 and #41, and not for #39, which still waits on #38.
- New, `in-progress-aside-jot-97-pause`: derived from the aside-jot#95 fixture with #100 merged. Nothing is offered.
- Every fixture now records its expected review comments and fixes, and gains the closed PR list. The dev-flow fixtures use the real lists as of their rewind time. The aside-jot ones weren't recorded and have empty lists, except where #100 is merged in derived states. #100's open and merge times weren't recorded either (this session can't read aside-jot), so I set them just after the review comment it answers. The fixture notes say so.

Plugin version 0.8.0 → 0.9.0. If #40's PR merges first with its own bump, I'll rebase onto it.

Closes #38

repos/kacxx/dev-flow/pulls?state=closed&.title: status reports an idea's stage and the next action (0.8.0)
repos/kacxx/dev-flow/pulls?state=closed&.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"kacxx"} -->
_Requested by **Kevin** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01MDcPXan8ZPVYF9Tu5iW7yq?thread=cmsg_01MDcPXan8ZPVYF9Tu5iW7yqBuF8bD6AatoTXiZiFaWmPM)_

Closes #37. Implements D1, D3, D4, D5, D7 of `docs/proposals/status.md`.

Before: to know where an idea is and what's next, the owner or an agent had to read the issue, its comments, the tickets, the doc PRs and the proposal doc, and reason it out.

After: `/dev-flow:status owner/repo#N` names the stage, the evidence for it, and the next action with who takes it, in the D3 four-part shape. It only reports; nothing is written.

**How.** `skills/status/scripts/state.py` reads the state through `gh api` (GET only) and prints one JSON object: `stage`, `evidence`, `also_matched`, `steps` (each with `who`: owner or agent), `next_action`, `later`, plus the tickets, doc PRs and doc it read. All nine D4 stages are recognised, and the first match in Shape 2's precedence order wins. `--record FILE` saves every response it read, which is the fixture format.

`test_state.py` replays one recorded fixture per stage, picked up by `run_tests.py`:

| Fixture | Source | Stage → next action |
|---|---|---|
| revision-in-progress-aside-jot-95 | aside-jot#95, rewound to before aside-jot#100 merged | revision in progress → merge aside-jot#100, then update #97–#99 |
| reopened | derived from the #95 fixture, #97 labelled `needs-decision` | settle the reopened decision in #97 with `grill` |
| done | aside-jot#78, live | close #78 |
| in progress | dev-flow#35, live | implement #37 |
| decided, full path | dev-flow#35 at #36's merge | run `to-tickets` on docs/proposals/status.md |
| proposal drafted | dev-flow#35 with #36 open at its first commit (D4 reopened there) | settle the reopened decision in dev-flow#36 with `grill` |
| decided, awaiting proposal | dev-flow#35 after the grill comment | write the proposal for #35 with `proposal` |
| decided, short path | aside-jot#103, live | implement #103 |
| questions open | aside-jot#30, live | answer #30's open questions with `grill` |

Each fixture's `note` says what was rewound. Unit tests cover the markers the fixtures don't (a code PR that says `Refs #N`, superseded `Status: reopened` lines, To check, skipped questions in a grill record).

Defaults where the decisions are silent:
- A `Status: reopened` line puts the idea in "reopened" only from the doc on `main`. One in a draft doc PR keeps it at "proposal drafted", with `grill` on that decision as the next action.
- A doc PR says `Refs`, `Closes` or `Fixes #N`, the forms `proposal` accepts.
- Skipped questions in a grill record are any items under an "Open questions" or "Skipped" heading in the latest record.
- Run on a ticket instead of the source issue, it matches no stage and names the parent to run it on.

For #39: the fixtures sit under `skills/status/scripts/` as Shape 4 says, so they ride along in the account-skill ZIP (about 400 KB). The build may want to leave out `fixtures/` and `test_*.py`.

README and the account-skill set are #39; the shared shape in the other skills is #40; the eval is #41.

## What
`skills/proposal` writes the decided design doc from an issue's decisions and fact-checks it. It's the review step for doc PRs in place of `/code-review`. Plugin bumped to **0.3.0**.

- **Sections:** Status, Problem, Decisions (`### D<n>`, superseded text kept), Shape, Fact-check (`Claim | Result | Source`), Out of scope, Risks.
- **Fact-check:** evidence in this order: a probe in the real environment, then source, then official docs, then third-party reports (⚠️). Every row has a source.
- **Consistency pass:** checks each decision against the others, and against Shape and the tests.
- **What blocks the merge:** a wrong claim, a contradiction or a skipped question reopens the decision (same ID; `grill` settles it). Unchecked facts a decision depends on also block.
- **Status:** exactly one of `decided` / `decided, M facts unchecked` / `N decisions open` / `N decisions open, M facts unchecked`.
- **The PR:** opened as a draft through REST until the doc is decided.
- **Existing work:** decisions left only in comments are folded into the doc, and an existing doc PR is updated rather than duplicated.

## Eval
See `evals/RESULTS.md`. Scores: catch-error **1.00** (baseline 0.00), consistency **1.00** (0.20), decided **0.87** (0.00).

**The ticket's D6 test:** given the same false claim in an unrelated project's decisions, it fetched Matt's actual `grilling` file, marked the claim ❌ ("asks in rounds", file cited), reopened the decision and kept the doc open, in 3/3 runs.

**Found while testing:**
- **The status line needed an exact grammar.** It once read "1 decision open — decided — 3 facts unchecked".
- **Unchecked facts needed a blocking state,** for the same reason `capture`'s To check blocks ready.

## What
`skills/grill`: frontier rounds adapted from Matt Pocock's `grilling` (MIT, credited in `NOTICE` at 49dd158). Plugin bumped to **0.2.0**, so installed copies update.

- **Facts first:** looks up `capture`'s **To check** facts with sub-agents before the first round. It never asks the owner for a fact.
- **Rounds:** asks every listed question at once, numbered, each with a recommendation worded so "yes" accepts it. A question it holds back gets a one-line reason (it depends on another answer, or a fact settled it). It never drops one silently.
- **Answers:** "yes" for all, or shorthand such as `1 yes, 2 no: X, 3 skip`.
- **Decisions:** recorded as `D<n>`, never reusing an ID, stating only what was accepted. Reopened decisions keep their ID, with the old text kept as superseded.
- **The record:** goes into the issue body on the short path, or one `## Decisions (grill, <date>)` comment on the full path, written through `gh api`.

## Eval
See `evals/RESULTS.md`.

- **Clearly better than no plugin:**
  - one round with every question accounted for: 3/3 vs 0/3
  - the accept-all/shorthand line: 3/3 vs 0/3
  - a recommendation per question: 3/3 vs 0/3
  - the record header: 3/3 vs 0/3
  - ID handling on mixed shorthand: 3/3 vs 0/3
- **Ticket test** (from #1's six questions, D1–D6 in one or two rounds): D1–D6 recorded 2/3 by the LLM judge, and `**D6:` present 3/3 by regex.

## Open
- **The `fidelity` grader:** it checks that decisions contain nothing beyond what was accepted, and it fails both arms in every run, while the outputs read as faithful on manual inspection. Either the grader is too strict or I'm missing something. Worth your eye on one output.

Implements: D1, D2, D5 — docs/proposals/idea-to-tickets.md
Refs #5

## What

- **Plugin:** `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and `plugin.json` (v0.1.0). `claude plugin validate` passes for the marketplace, the plugin and the skills.
- **`capture` skill:**
  - Checks for an existing issue or PR on the same idea.
  - Drafts Problem / Idea / Open questions, where Idea says *what* changes, not *how*.
  - Lists facts it couldn't look up under **To check**, kept apart from the open questions.
  - Picks the D2 path (ready / short / full), states the reason and offers a one-word override.
  - Posts through `gh api` once the owner approves.
- **`NOTICE`:** Matt Pocock's MIT notice, byte-identical to his LICENSE.
- **`evals/`:** three `claude plugin eval` cases, one per path, on aside-jot ideas. Results are gitignored.

## Eval results

3 runs per case, Sonnet judge, compared with a no-plugin baseline:

| Case | Path correct | Shape | Score (baseline) |
|---|---|---|---|
| ready | 3/3 | 3/3 | 1.00 (0) |
| short | 3/3 | 1/3 | 0.67 (0) |
| full | 3/3 | 0/3 | 0.50 (0) |

- **Path selection:** 9/9 with the plugin, 0/9 without.
- **Open:** on short and full ideas, the Idea section adds reasonable details of its own (e.g. "show the evidence", "never close without asking"), and the shape grader counts those as settling the *how*. Either the skill should push them into Open questions, or the grader is too strict. That's the owner's call.

## Changes made along the way

- **Grader fixes:** the first grader was overfitted to #1's six questions, and the first case let the repo leak in. The ready path legitimately states its fix, and user-stated constraints don't count as design.
- **Skill fixes from the evals:** "what not how" for Idea, and the To check list.
